title: The Aggregation Paradox
hook: Your overall numbers look great. Your segments might be telling a completely different story.
statement: A trend can hold in every single group and still flip once you lump the groups together.
explainer: When groups are different sizes and start from different baselines, the overall number can point the wrong way. Something can win in every segment and still lose overall.
sop: Split your headline number into its segments.
Check if each segment's trend matches the total.
Look for what's skewing how the segments are weighted.
Rate Segment Mix Imbalance from 1 to 10.
When it's high, decide from the segments, not the total.
equation_example: One segment is 90% of your volume with a low base rate, the other 10% with a high one. That's a Segment Mix Imbalance of about 8. At 8 to 10, trust the segment numbers. At 1 to 3, the total is safe to read.
question: Take your top metric and break it down by customer type. Note whether the trend flips.
closing_statement: The truth usually lives one level below the headline.
caption:
Principle Nº 351: The Aggregation Paradox

Your overall numbers look great. Your segments might be telling a completely different story.

A trend can hold in every single group and still flip once you lump the groups together.

Your turn: Take your top metric and break it down by customer type. Note whether the trend flips.
